description: We are a team with backgrounds in Full-Stack Software Engineering, Game Development, and Robotics & AI, tackling the Space Mission Design Game challenge. Our goal is to build an interactive, browser playable simulator grounded in real NASA aerospace trade-offs challenging players to balance mass, power, budget, communications, and orbital constraints from mission concept to operation. Our team roster is complete for this edition.
summary:
AstraRex is an interactive 3D Lunar South Pole mission engineering simulator built in Godot 4 that puts players in command of a robotic lander mission to Shackleton Crater. Bridging the Space Mission Design Game, AstraRex transforms abstract aerospace trade-offs into hands-on systems engineering across four continuous phases: Mission Formulation, 3D Modular Vehicle Assembly, Physics-Driven Powered Descent, and Multi-Objective Pareto Debriefing.

Grounded in official NASA engineering handbooks, ephemerides, altimetry, and radiation telemetry, AstraRex solves a critical STEM and mission-planning gap: students and aspiring engineers rarely experience how mass growth allowances, Tsiolkovsky delta-v, thrust-to-weight ratios, power budgets, and a fixed $350M cost cap interact simultaneously. Featuring one-click presets, a Student/Engineer SI toggle, and CSV/JSON telemetry export, AstraRex runs directly in any browser without installation.
details:
AstraRex is an interactive 3D space mission engineering simulator built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 (Space Mission Design Game). Targeting the Lunar South Pole around Shackleton Crater (89.54° S, 129.17° E), it lets players design, assemble, land, and optimize a lunar lander across four connected phases from mission formulation to post-flight Pareto analysis directly in any desktop browser:

- Phase 1 (Mission Formulation): Players define a scientific objective (Polar Ice Assay, PSR Radar Mapping, or Ridge Precursor), choose a South Pole landing zone, assign up to four asymmetric team roles, and pair a launch vehicle with a transfer orbit (LLO 100 km Polar or NRHO Gateway).

- Phase 2 (3D VAB Assembly): Players snap modular subsystems bus, chemical or Hall-effect propulsion, articulated solar arrays or Pu-238 MMRTG, cryogenic batteries, Ka/S-Band DSN antennas, Rad-Hard vs. COTS avionics, LiDAR TRN, scientific payloads (TRIDENT, MSolo, Mini-RF SAR), and radiation shielding onto a 3D chassis while inspecting live non-mutating ±Mass, ±Power, ±Δv, and ±Cost trade deltas before clearing the System Integration Review (SIR).

- Phase 3 (Lunar Sim): Executes an accelerated terminal descent and surface operations over real LRO LOLA 16-bit elevation terrain, using RayCast3D solar grazing shadows (88.5°) and Earth Direct-to-Earth visibility driven by JPL Horizons (DE441), alongside OSDR RadLab 24-hour Solar Particle Event (SPE) storms and Safe Mode load shedding.

- Phase 4 (Pareto Debrief): Computes the multi-objective Pareto Frontier (Science Return vs. Wet Mass, Cost, and Survival), diagnoses physical failure root causes, and exports shareable Base64 design codes plus CSV/JSON reports.

To deliver authentic educational and engineering impact, AstraRex enforces real International System (SI) physics rather than arbitrary game bars applying NASA SP-2016-6105 Rev2 lifecycle gates (Pre-Phase A through Phase E), Mass Growth Allowance (15%–20% MGA), the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, a hard lunar T/W >= 1.0 landing lockout (g_moon = 1.625 m/s²), CLPS mission cost envelopes, and ionizing dose attenuation, and NASA/JPL Concept Maturity Levels (CML 1-4) alongside the 4 Mission Segments from Design and Develop Science Missions. A zero-layout-shift Student / Engineer (SI) toggle makes complex trade-offs intuitive for learners while giving technical users exact SI telemetry and exportable baselines, complemented by one-click judge presets (P1 Optimal, P2 Failure, P3 Sandbox) for evaluation.

Creatively, AstraRex merges an industrial Mission Control HUD, clickable 3D VAB callout pins, real-time topographically grounded South Pole raycast shadowing, procedural 44.1 kHz Apollo Quindar and telemetry Web Audio, and an interactive Pareto Frontier solver inside one cohesive 1280×720 console.

We built AstraRex in Godot 4.7.2 (GL Compatibility / WebGL2), supported by a audio synthesis pipeline and Blender mesh optimization for NASA 3D Resources .glb models. The simulator Boots in Itch.io, and standard browser iframes the zip file size is about 13 Mb.
